title: Meet the Ekho AI Website: the dealer site you change by asking
summary: The Ekho Website is a dealer website you build and change by asking, with live inventory, all-in pricing, publish checks, roles, domains and AI agent access built in. We are onboarding our first dealers now.
body_markdown:
Summary


The Ekho Website is a dealer website you build and change by asking, with live inventory, all-in pricing, publish checks, roles, domains and AI agent access built in. We are onboarding our first dealers now.


Today we are introducing the Ekho Website: a dealer website you build, change and run by asking for what you want. Tell it to add a section, rewrite a page or move your newest arrivals to the top of Home, and it does it on your draft in seconds. Nothing goes live until you publish, and every publish passes the same checks for pricing, accessibility and your manufacturer's rules.


We are onboarding our first dealers now, by hand, across automotive and powersports. If you want to be one of them,[book a demo](https://www.ekho.com/book-a-demo) and we will walk you through it on your own inventory.


The clip above is real and unedited apart from speed. A dealer asks for a way to browse by type under the hero, Ekho reads the site, checks the change against the site's rules, and adds the section. The change card on the right shows exactly what moved, with an Undo beside it.


##


What dealers told us about their websites


Before we wrote a line of code, we listened. Over the last year our team has sat through dozens of calls with dealers and dealer groups, and the website came up in almost all of them. Rarely as something they liked.


The same complaints came up again and again. Dealers stay on sites they do not like because of annual contracts and co-op programs that only reimburse approved vendors. Their sites look like every other store on the same template. A new technology director at one auto group put it plainly: the website was the only legacy piece left in their stack. Changing anything means a support ticket and a wait, and inventory and photo updates can take a day to show up. Several dealers told us their provider was acquired, their support rep now covers hundreds of stores, and service got worse. Others could not see their own traffic.


Most of all, the site stops at the lead form. A shopper finds a car, fills in a form, and the deal leaves the website for a phone call, a separate chat tool on each brand's site, and a desk that starts from zero. Meanwhile more than 60% of buyers browse after 5 PM, when the doors are closed (NADA), and about 30% of in-market buyers now use AI search to research their next vehicle (Ekho study, 2026). A template site built for a search engine from ten years ago is not ready for either.


We built the Ekho Website to fix those problems, not to give dealers another template.


##


Change your site by asking


Think of the way Shopify® made an online store something a merchant could run alone, or the way Lovable turns a sentence into a working app. The Ekho Website brings that to a dealership, with the inventory, pricing rules and compliance a dealership needs built in.


Ask for a change and Ekho makes it on your draft. Every answer comes with a change card you can undo. Apex Auto is a demo dealership.


The editor is your site, live, with Ask Ekho beside it. You can ask in plain English, click any section to change it, or type straight onto the page. Ekho already knows your business details, your rooftops, your inventory and your brands, so it writes for your store rather than a generic one. It cannot change a price or a legal disclosure, because those come from your inventory and your compliance settings, not from the page.


Every change is saved as a version. You can preview any earlier version, pick up the conversation that made it, or restore it in one click.


Every change is a version you can preview, reopen in chat or restore.


##


Make it yours


Your site should look like your store, not like your provider's catalog. Themes set your colors, fonts, corners and spacing once, and every page follows. Light and dark themes are both checked for contrast before they can go live. Sections come from a library built for dealers, with hero layouts, featured inventory, shop by type and by model, reviews, team pages, FAQs and more, and Ekho can write a custom section when the library does not have what you want.


One theme sets colors, type, corners and spacing for every page.


##


Built around your inventory


Every page reads your live inventory. When a vehicle arrives, it gets its own page, its place in search, and a spot in your Google and Meta vehicle feeds without anyone touching the site. When it sells, it comes down. Search results, vehicle pages and the rows on your home page all draw from the same inventory, so they never disagree.


A home page written for the store, with search and live inventory under the hero.Vehicle pages with a full photo tour, built from the listing with no manual work.


##


Compliance is part of the page


Advertised pricing is where dealer websites get dealers into trouble, so we made it impossible to get wrong by accident. Every card and every vehicle page shows one all-in price with the dealer fees already in it, and a shopper can open the breakdown. The monthly payment shows its terms. These parts of the page are sealed: no editor, no theme and no AI change can remove them. It is all designed to align with the FTC's guidance on advertised prices, which we wrote about in[whole price on every vehicle page](https://www.ekho.com/blog/ftc-whole-price-on-every-vehicle-page) .


The all-in price on every card, with the breakdown one tap away. Prices and fees are illustrative.Price, payment, fees and next steps on every vehicle page, with pre-qualification that does not touch the buyer's credit.


Every site also comes with an accessibility statement, privacy and terms pages, cookie consent and a privacy choices page, and the rules for your state and your manufacturer's certification program. Before anything goes live, Ekho runs the publish checks: every page renders, no link is broken, text and buttons meet contrast, images have alt text, prices display correctly, and your OEM's co-op rules are met. A change that breaks a pricing rule is left out of the publish, and the rest goes live.


Publish shows what is waiting to go live and whether every check passes.


##


Decide who can change what


Most dealerships have more than one person who should touch the website, and not all of them should be able to publish it. Each person gets a role on the site: view, edit drafts, publish, or owner. Your marketing manager can edit drafts all day, your general manager approves anything that changes how prices display, and your agency gets exactly the access you give it. The same rules apply in the editor, in Ask Ekho and to any AI agent acting for someone, so a token can never do more than the person who made it.


##


Your own domain, bought or connected in minutes


Every site gets an Ekho address the moment it is created, so you can share a preview before anything else is set up. When you are ready, buy a new domain through Ekho and it is registered to your business and connected for you, or connect a domain you already own. Ekho tells you exactly which records to change, checks them for you, and turns on the secure connection by itself.


Buy a domain through Ekho, or bring one you already own.Every address in one list, with its status.Connected, with the secure connection turned on for you.


##


A garage for every shopper


Shoppers can save the vehicles they like as they browse, with no account and no form, and compare them side by side. Saved vehicles carry their price, so when a price drops or a vehicle sells, the shopper can hear about it, and a shopper who sets an alert on a search hears when a match arrives. Every alert is opt-in and records the shopper's consent, and the leads it brings back go to your CRM like any other.


Save, compare and come back. The header keeps count.


##


Images when you need them


A dealer website lives or dies on its photos, and most stores do not have a photographer for every banner and landing page. Ekho can generate the images a section needs, from a seasonal hero to a service banner, and save them to your site's media library for you to approve. Vehicles that have not been photographed yet get a clean scene with their details instead of a "photo coming soon" placeholder, until the real photos arrive.


##


Open to AI agents: yours, your agency's and your buyers'


Every Ekho Website can be read and worked on by AI agents, through the open Model Context Protocol (MCP) that the major assistants support. That works in two directions.


Your buyers' assistants can shop your site. When a buyer asks ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or Perplexity to find them a car, those assistants can search your inventory, look up a vehicle with its itemized price, get your hours and locations, send you a lead with the buyer's consent recorded, and hand the buyer to your Sales Agent. They see the same vehicles and the same all-in prices your site shows, and you choose what they can do.


Your own agents can work on it. You, your marketing team or your agency can connect a coding agent such as Claude Code or Codex, or your own personal AI assistant, and ask it to update the site. Every change it makes lands on your draft, shows up in the publish dialog with the agent's name on it, and passes the same checks as a change made in the editor.


You choose what buyers' AI assistants can do on your site.


##


A site that keeps itself current


A website should not need a person to keep it accurate. Ekho runs routines on every site: new vehicles are added and sold ones are taken down, expired promotions come off the pages they were on, past events roll off, and your Google Business Profile is checked against your details. Anything that changes data that was already approved goes live by itself. Anything that changes words or pages waits for someone with permission to publish.


##


One platform, from the first click to the delivered car


The Ekho Website is not a standalone site with a chat box bolted on. It runs on the same platform as the[AI Sales Agent](https://www.ekho.com/sales-agent) and the[Transaction Engine](https://www.ekho.com/transaction-engine) , so every part of the buying experience is connected.


The AI Sales Agent answers on every page, at any hour, and knows the vehicle the shopper is looking at. Trade-in, test drive and contact forms run through it, so every lead lands in your CRM with its full context instead of a bare email. Pre-qualification takes a shopper to their real terms without touching their credit. And on any vehicle you sell online, Buy online carries the shopper into the Transaction Engine's checkout: financing, protection products, paperwork, signatures, titling and registration. 70% of Ekho online buyers say they probably or definitely would not have bought without the online option, so this is business your store would not otherwise have had.


##


Moving off your current provider


Switching websites is the part dealers dread, so we built the move to do the work for you. Ekho reads your current site, pulls your logo, colors and fonts, sorts your pages, maps your forms to Ekho flows, matches your inventory and builds a redirect for every old URL so you keep your search rankings and your saved links. It only reads public pages, it never logs in to your old provider, and your old site stays live until you point your domain at Ekho.


##


We are onboarding our first dealers now


We are rolling the Ekho Website out to a small group of dealers across automotive and powersports, starting with stores that already use Ekho, and onboarding each one by hand. If your website contract is coming up, your site has not changed in years, or you are tired of filing a ticket to change a banner, we would like to talk.


[Book a demo](https://www.ekho.com/book-a-demo) and we will show you the Ekho Website on your own inventory, or[read more about the Ekho Website](https://www.ekho.com/website) .
